clue.text: Scrapes part of sleeve in case of shingles

indicators.note: in signals that the sleeve part sits inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: a cuff is the end part of a sleeve

explanation.surface: A doctor notes scratches on someone's arm from a bout of shingles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of shingles' gives the outer letters S and S, which hold CUFF. Shingles is a painful viral rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: scuffs as a verb means grazes or marks a surface by scraping.

clue.text: Beginning to collect bids for chests

indicators.note: the beginning of the word collect is just its opening letter

parts.note: bids are offers made at auction

explanation.surface: An auctioneer starts gathering bids for some antique chests.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: coffers are strongboxes or chests for holding money and valuables.

clue.text: Pressure exerted on behalf of the church

parts.note: acting for someone is acting on their behalf
CE is short for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone complains of pressure being applied in the name of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in physics and everyday speech, a push or pressure applied to something is a force.

clue.text: Lazy, and lacking a work pattern

parts.note: a shift is a pattern or period of working hours
the suffix less means lacking

explanation.surface: Someone is called idle because they have no regular rota at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a shiftless person is idle and lacking ambition or effort.

clue.text: Boss of kitchen finishes early, admitting a problem

indicators.note: admitting means letting the letter in, so it goes inside
finishing early means stopping before the last letter

parts.note: the head chef runs a restaurant kitchen

explanation.surface: The head chef leaves before closing time and owns up to a difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes early' trims HEAD CHEF to HEADCHE; 'admitting' puts A inside it after HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a headache is a nagging problem or source of worry.

clue.text: 'Ton' that was once part of a county?

definitions.meaning: a ton is slang for a century

definitions.text: that was once part of a county
definitions.meaning: historically English counties were divided into administrative districts called ...

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: slang for the number one hundred, and an old subdivision of an English shire.

clue.text: Improve notice when employing workers

indicators.note: employing means taking in, so the workers go inside the notice

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
men are workers, as in hired hands

explanation.surface: A firm posts a better job advertisement when it takes on staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to amend a text is to correct or improve it.

clue.text: Disaffected foreigner on date getting confused

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner

indicators.note: getting confused means the letters of date are jumbled

explanation.surface: A disgruntled visitor from abroad gets muddled on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is only positional here: the jumble of date, made by 'getting confused', comes after the foreigner.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone alienated feels estranged or disaffected.

clue.text: Egg producer's embargo on eastern plant that's poisonous

parts.note: a hen lays eggs
an embargo is a ban

explanation.surface: A chicken is banned from a toxic eastern plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: henbane is a toxic nightshade-family herb, historically used as a poison.

clue.text: Go in feeling jittery about other ranks in military unit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the ranks
jittery means nervous and shaky, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, the non-officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers who are not officers go in nervously to join a unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jittery' scrambles GO IN FEELING, and 'about' wraps those letters round OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the French Foreign Legion is a famous army unit of foreign volunteers.

clue.text: Person who goes over fault with unprotected work

parts.note: a defect is a fault

indicators.note: unprotected strips off the outer letters, leaving the middle of work

explanation.surface: Someone crosses over with a flaw in their unguarded work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes over' means switches sides, not checks something.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to go over to the enemy is to change allegiance, which a turncoat does.

clue.text: Rejection of trade across Northern Ireland

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the trade word stretches round the province

parts.note: a deal is a trade

explanation.surface: A trade arrangement covering Northern Ireland is turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a denial is a refusal or rejection of something.

clue.text: Remains with mineral deposit on dry land

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
ore is a natural deposit of mineral

explanation.surface: Ashes and some rock are left on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something washed up is on the shore, out of the water.

clue.text: High season will be issue

parts.note: high food, like meat that has gone bad, is off
spring is a season

explanation.surface: The peak season will be a talking point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means children, not a topic or a magazine number.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: issue in its legal sense means children or descendants.

clue.text: Fans of referendum among rejected children

indicators.note: among means set inside the other piece
rejected means sent back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring
a referendum is a public vote

explanation.surface: Supporters of a public poll find themselves among cast-off youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SEED into DEES, which surrounds VOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: devotees are keen followers or enthusiasts of something.

clue.text: Loved changes with capital for sports venue

indicators.note: changes signals the letters of loved are rearranged

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: Someone beloved changes cities to visit a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loved' looks like the start of the story, but 'changes' makes it anagram fodder; 'with' simply joins the Italian capital on.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a velodrome is a banked track arena for cycle racing.

clue.text: Prisoner joined out of order

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
fused means joined together

explanation.surface: An inmate is linked to someone in a jumbled sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: things confused are muddled and in disarray.

clue.text: Work on outsize problem for an animal

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Someone tackles an oversized puzzle about a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an opossum is an American marsupial mammal.

clue.text: In cold wind leaves get smaller

indicators.note: In signals the letters sit within the next three words

explanation.surface: A chilly breeze makes the foliage shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dwindle is to shrink gradually.

clue.text: Run in hose — it's needed by firemen

definitions.meaning: a run in tights or stockings is a vertical tear
firefighters climb up these to reach blazes

explanation.surface: A hosepipe springs a leak, and the fire crew needs equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' means stockings, not a firefighter's water pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a snag in hosiery, and the climbing frame of rungs used by fire crews.

clue.text: Organs stolen may be visible within this

parts.note: eyes are organs of sight
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Stolen body parts might be seen from close by.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: within sight range is the distance the eye can see.

clue.text: Expected to eat quietly, but jumped

indicators.note: to eat means to take something inside

parts.note: hoped means expected or wished
p is the musical sign for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Someone was expected to dine in silence but leapt up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hopped means leapt or sprang.

clue.text: Excitement caused by whisky with a chaser?

indicators.note: a chaser follows, so the letter comes after the whisky

parts.note: a dram is a measure of whisky

explanation.surface: A dram of whisky followed by a beer causes a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: A chaser is a drink taken after spirits; here it says A follows DRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: drama means excitement or commotion, as in making a fuss.

clue.text: Under an obligation, actually accepting telephone company

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the company goes inside

parts.note: indeed means in fact, actually
BT is British Telecom, the UK phone company

explanation.surface: Someone owes a debt, actually taking on a phone contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being in debt or owing gratitude means you are under an obligation.

clue.text: Pipe or rail oddly found in pub

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of rail

explanation.surface: A pipe or railing turns up mysteriously in a tavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks R and I from rail, which go inside BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a briar is a tobacco pipe carved from heath root.

clue.text: Endless rancour, with European smartness

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: spite is rancour or malice
and means with or plus
Polish means from Poland, a European country

explanation.surface: Bitter ill will meets a person from the continent's neat appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase means meticulous cleaning and smartness, especially in military dress.

clue.text: Leave the country for golf in Dubai, say

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the state

parts.note: Dubai is an example of an emirate
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone moves abroad to play golf in the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to emigrate is to depart one's homeland to live elsewhere.

clue.text: Flyers, for example, and engineers regularly failing in test

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: regularly failing means every other letter of test drops out

explanation.surface: Pilots and engineers keep failing an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly failing in' keeps T and S from test.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: egrets are white herons, birds that fly.
